meta.title: Expedition Log
meta.subtitle: Twenty charted voyages — an Odyssey across the stars and the deep universe

expeditions.title: The First Crossing
expeditions.premise: Every odyssey begins with leaving harbour. The shortest possible voyage between suns — and still four years at a tenth of light.

stops.note: Home port. Cast off.
The nearest star of all — a faint red ember with a world in its warmth.
Alpha Centauri, the bright twin next door. The far shore of the first crossing.

expeditions.title: The Sirian Run
expeditions.premise: A trader's dash to the brightest star in the sky and back along the Dog's track.

stops.note: Departure.
The Dog Star — blue-white and blinding, with a white-dwarf companion.
The Little Dog. A short reach completes the run.

expeditions.title: The Winter Beacons
expeditions.premise: Navigate by the great winter lights, the beacons sailors have steered by for ten thousand years.

stops.note: First beacon.
Second beacon.
The Twin's head.
The She-Goat, a golden lantern to close the circuit.

expeditions.title: Errand of the Red Giants
expeditions.premise: An old captain's pilgrimage to the swollen suns — stars near the end of their lives, burning orange and vast.

stops.note: Set out.
The Bull's fiery eye.
A giant with a planet, quietly.
The Bear-Watcher, racing through the halo of the galaxy.

expeditions.title: The Lantern Circuit
expeditions.premise: Chart the Summer Triangle — three lanterns that ride the Milky Way's river of light.

stops.note: The Harp Star, once and future pole star.
The Eagle, spinning so fast it bulges at the waist.
The Lonely One of the south, ringed with debris. A wide tack home.

expeditions.title: Voyage to the Galactic Heart
expeditions.premise: Inward, past the glowing nurseries of the Milky Way, to the monster that anchors it all.

stops.label: Sol
stops.note: Leave the harbour of home.
A stellar nursery — stars being born in the dark.
Toward the crowded core, clouds lit from within.
The heart: four million suns of black hole, silent at the centre.

expeditions.title: The Nebula Pilgrimage
expeditions.premise: A slow tour of the great clouds — where stars are made and where they are unmade.

stops.note: The nursery of Orion's sword.
The Pillars of Creation stand here.
A vast southern furnace around a doomed star.
A dying sun's smoke ring — a glimpse of the Sun's own future.

expeditions.title: Graveyard of Giants
expeditions.premise: Sail the wrecks of exploded stars — supernova remnants still expanding centuries after the blast.

stops.note: The wreck of a star seen to explode in 1054 AD.
An older ruin, sheets of glowing filament.
The youngest remnant in the galaxy, still ringing.
The star Tycho Brahe watched blaze and fade.

expeditions.title: The Lighthouse Keepers
expeditions.premise: Among the pulsars — neutron stars sweeping the void with beams, the most precise clocks in nature.

stops.note: Spinning thirty times a second inside the Crab.
A younger lighthouse, glitching as it slows.
A silent gamma-ray beacon, radio-quiet.
The first pulsar ever found — once nicknamed LGM-1.

expeditions.title: Sirens of the Deep
expeditions.premise: Heed the sirens and live: a run past black holes, from a stellar-mass killer to the titan in another galaxy.

stops.note: The first black hole ever confirmed, feeding on a blue giant.
A restless X-ray nova, flaring without warning.
Our galaxy's central engine.
The first black hole ever imaged — six billion suns, in another galaxy entirely.

expeditions.title: The Andromeda Passage
expeditions.premise: Leave the Milky Way behind. Cross the dark between galaxies to our great neighbour and its court.

stops.label: Milky Way
stops.note: Our own island of stars.
A ragged companion galaxy, close astern.
Its smaller twin, streaming a bridge of gas.
The great spiral, on a collision course with home — in four billion years.

expeditions.title: Grand Tour of the Island Universes
expeditions.premise: The old name for galaxies was island universes. Visit the most beautiful islands in the nearby sea.

stops.note: A grand-design spiral, dancing with a small companion.
Edge-on, a brim of dust across a glowing bulge.
A vast, near-perfect face-on pinwheel.
A giant elliptical shooting a jet thousands of light-years long.
A ring of fire — a galaxy struck dead-centre and left ringing.

expeditions.title: The Local Group Odyssey
expeditions.premise: Round the whole Local Group — every major galaxy bound to ours by gravity across three million light-years.

stops.note: Companion.
The great spiral.
The third-largest of the group.
Just past the edge — a grand spiral and its starburst partner.
A warped elliptical with a dust lane, a black hole roaring at its core.

expeditions.title: Wanderers of the Sculptor Wall
expeditions.premise: South, along the thin bridge of galaxies in Sculptor — the nearest filament of the cosmic web.

stops.note: A bright, dusty starburst spiral.
A delicate, flocculent spiral nearby.
A faint dwarf orbiting the Milky Way.
The next town on the web — a small cluster of galaxies.

expeditions.title: Climb to the Great Attractor
expeditions.premise: Everything nearby is falling one way. Follow the current up the ladder of clusters toward what pulls us.

stops.note: The heart of our own supercluster, a thousand galaxies.
A rich cluster on the road down the slope.
The gravitational lowpoint we are all falling toward.
Our home supercluster — 'immense heaven' — and its watershed.

expeditions.title: The Shapley Expedition
expeditions.premise: Beyond the Attractor lies something greater still — the largest concentration of mass in the nearby universe.

stops.note: A dense, round cluster — where dark matter was first inferred.
A chain of clusters strung along the web.
The great overdensity — the destination the current has been pointing to.

expeditions.title: Along the Sloan Great Wall
expeditions.premise: Sail the largest structures ever mapped — walls of galaxies over a billion light-years long, and the emptiness beside them.

stops.note: The near end of the walls.
The first 'great wall' discovered — a sheet of galaxies.
Even larger — 1.4 billion light-years of galaxies.
And beside it, the Great Nothing — a bubble almost empty of galaxies.

expeditions.title: Into the Quasar Age
expeditions.premise: Look outward and you look backward. Sail toward the quasars — young galaxies blazing in the early universe.

stops.note: The first quasar identified — brilliant across two billion light-years.
A blazar, its jet aimed almost straight at us.
A gravitationally-lensed beacon in the deep field.
A quasar from when the universe was young — a supermassive black hole that shouldn't yet exist.

expeditions.title: To the Edge of the Observable
expeditions.premise: The longest voyage of all — outward through every scale until the map itself ends at the first light of the Big Bang.

stops.label: Sol
stops.note: Home, at the centre of all we can see.
The nearest great galaxy.
The nearest great cluster.
The nearest great supercluster.
The largest wall of galaxies.
A quasar near the dawn of galaxies.

stops.label: CMB horizon
stops.note: The edge: the microwave glow of the Big Bang, the farthest we can ever see.

expeditions.title: The Ulysses Circuit
expeditions.premise: Like Ulysses, wander far and come home changed. A grand loop through the landmarks of the deep — and back to the heart of the Milky Way.

stops.note: Cast off from the galactic heart.
Cross to the neighbour spiral.
Round a distant, beautiful island.
Climb into the great cluster.
Ride the current to the Attractor.
Glimpse a quasar's fire at the turn of the voyage.
And home at last — the long way round.

expeditions.title: The Titans' Road
expeditions.premise: A pilgrimage to the true giants near home — supergiant suns hundreds of light-years off, any one of which could swallow the orbit of Jupiter whole.

stops.note: Cast off from a very ordinary star.
The Bull's eye — an orange giant, close and warm.
Orion's red shoulder, a doomed supergiant that could go supernova any millennium.
Orion's blue-white foot — 120,000 times the Sun's light.
The Heart of the Scorpion, a vast red supergiant.
The Swan's tail — among the most luminous stars known, 1,400 ly out.

expeditions.title: Walking Orion
expeditions.premise: The hunter is a trick of perspective. Fly the stars of Orion and watch the familiar figure fall apart — they lie at wildly different distances, bound only by our line of sight.

stops.note: The left shoulder — nearest of the bright ones, ~250 ly.
The right shoulder, red, ~500 ly.
The Belt's eastern star, a hot triple ~740 ly off.
The Belt's centre — a blue supergiant nearly 2,000 ly away.
The right knee, ~650 ly.
The left foot, ~860 ly. Nothing here truly stands beside its neighbour.

expeditions.title: The Open-Cluster Run
expeditions.premise: Hop between the nearby open clusters — loose swarms of young sibling stars, born together and slowly drifting apart.

stops.note: The nearest cluster of all, the Bull's face.
The Seven Sisters, blue and veiled in dust.
A rich swarm in Cancer, a naked-eye smudge.
A bright, sprawling group around Mirfak.

expeditions.title: The Deep Descent
expeditions.premise: Not a flyby — a descent. Cross to the great galaxies and drop inside each one, among its own hundred billion suns, before rising back into the dark. (Cruise it — each ⛶ stop lands you inside.)

stops.label: Milky Way
stops.note: Leave home.
Descend into the great spiral — fly among the stars of another galaxy.
Drop into the third-largest island of the Local Group.
Down into the Whirlpool's grand-design arms.
Rise, and end before the giant of Virgo and its jet.

expeditions.title: The Island Landings
expeditions.premise: An explorer's log of landings — touch down inside our companion galaxies, from the ragged Magellanic Clouds to the great spiral next door. (Cruise it to land inside each.)

stops.note: Land in the Large Magellanic Cloud, its Tarantula Nebula ablaze.
Cross to its smaller twin.
The long jump — inside Andromeda itself.
Home again, at the black heart of the Milky Way.
